summary: Boot order randomizes after Dell BIOS secure-erase flow, preventing OS redeploy during depot repair
description:
Issue summary: Several depot-repair units after SSD secure-erase (NVM-erase flow invoked by depot technicians) are entering a state where UEFI boot order is effectively randomized. Impact: Devices fail to find the SCCM/WinPE network PXE entry and drop back to local drive or USB first, preventing automated OS redeploy and blocking depot turnaround. This affects staging depot workflow and has increased manual intervention by ~40% this week.

Observed behavior: Post secure-erase and firmware finalization step, firmware reports a boot order with incorrect GUID ordering; PXE entry is pushed to bottom of list intermittently. On some units the onboard NVMe presents a different device GUID which causes UEFI to prefer it ahead of network boot.

Expected behavior: After secure-erase and firmware finalize step, boot entries should retain the configured PXE/USB/SSD ordering required by our task sequence so automated redeploy can proceed.

Environment: Staging depot rack, BIOS images from vendor signed package (version 1.14.2), our depot task-sequence v2026.03.01, SCCM PXE service point in us-west, affected models listed above.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Acquire Dell Precision 5560 with fresh NVMe installed
2) Boot to depot-prep USB and run secure-erase utility (vendor NVMe secure erase via nvme-cli wrapper) as part of depot-repair flow
3) Apply BIOS firmware package 1.14.2 and run "finalize-firmware" script that resets NVRAM and writes boot entries via vendor tool
4) Reboot and let device go to PXE. Observe Boot Menu ordering and PXE success/failure
5) Repeat 5–10 times across multiple units to observe variability
logs: Firmware event log excerpt: BootEntry(0003): 4C454E-... GUID shifted to position 7 after NVRAM reset
System journal from device-2026-03-09-10: nvme-cli: secure-erase successful, return code 0
Depot script debug: finalize-firmware: wrote 8 boot entries, exit 0
SCCM server: PXE request not received from client; client timed out waiting for network boot
investigation_notes: 03/10 - Initial triage by depot techs: reproduced on 3/12 units, not on all units of same model. Pattern: occurs after nvme secure-erase followed by BIOS flash+NVRAM reset.

03/11 - Confirmed BIOS package 1.14.2 contains NVRAM reset that uses vendor API to clear BootOrder. Hypothesis: vendor API enumerates devices by GUID after an erase and assigns boot order based on enumeration order which is non-deterministic when NVMe VID/PID are identical.
03/11 - Cross-checked with Dell release notes: no known bug matching random boot order but noted change in NVRAM init behavior in 1.14.x series.
03/12 - Recreated on a lab unit: running vendor finalize-firmware with 'preserve-boot' flag avoided reorder. Running without flag triggers issue.
03/12 - Correlated with asset-db: units with re-encoded serials after depot swap are slightly more likely to exhibit problem (~65% of repros).
comments: Asha Menon (Reporter) 2026-03-10: Ticket opened after depot reported 7/18 units failed automated redeploy this morning.
Liam Chen (Assignee) 2026-03-11: I will attempt lab repro and capture UEFI variables (efivar -l) before/after finalize-firmware. Need 2 test units reserved.
Depot Tech (Jamie R.) 2026-03-11: Confirmed we used the standard nvme-cli secure-erase wrapper; attaching screenshots to Confluence runbook (link below).
Liam Chen 2026-03-12: Repro succeeded in lab - vendor tool call to 'reset_nvm' enumerates GUIDs based on PCI bus ordering which changes after secure-erase. Filing vendor bridge request.
SRE (Marina P.) 2026-03-12: Temporary mitigation: add 'preserve-boot' flag to finalize-firmware in depot pipeline; please confirm no side effects with firmware validation step.
temporary_mitigation: Updated depot finalize-firmware script to run with 'preserve-boot' flag (depot branch: depot-patches/keep-boot-334455).
If preserve-boot flag is not present, depot script now verifies PXE entry at boot using an automated ACPI/UEFI check and will mark unit for manual fix instead of allowing redeploy to fail downstream.
Notified depot leads and added checklist item: validate PXE presence after finalize-firmware step
resolution_notes: 03/13 - Vendor escalated (Dell case #123456789). Vendor acknowledges non-deterministic enumeration in BIOS 1.14.x and provided hotfix package 1.14.3 that preserves boot entry ordering or exposes 'preserve-boot' flag in their finalize call.
03/13 - Applied 1.14.3 to two lab units and ran full depot flow 10x: no repro.
03/14 - Rolled hotfix to staging depot (canary: 10 units). Monitoring redeploy rate. If stable for 48 hours, plan full rollout and update depot runbook to include firmware hotfix version requirement.
Follow-ups: update asset-db reconciliation logic to avoid re-encoding serials unnecessarily during depot swap; open internal change request to ensure vendor flag is used in future firmware flows.
